spans.s: स्कन्द् 1. स्कन्द् = rt. स्कुन्द्, q. v.

स्कन्द् 2. स्कन्द् (also written स्कन्ध्), cl.
10. P. स्कन्दयति, स्कन्दायति, &c., to
collect.

स्कन्द् 3. स्कन्द् (connected with rt. स्कुन्द्,
q. v.), cl. 1. P. स्कन्दति (also A. -ते),
चस्कन्द (2nd sing. चस्कन्दिथ or चस्कन्त्थ),
स्कन्त्स्यति, अस्कदत् or अस्कान्त्सीत्, स्कन्त्तुम्, to
leap, jump, spring; to jump or spring upwards, rise,
mount, ascend; to raise (A., but in this sense re-
garded as a form of rt. स्कुन्द्); to jump down-
wards, drop, fall; to leap out, shoot out, burst out,
drop out, be poured out, be spilled, ooze; to go,
move, approach; to fall away; to perish (A.); to
become dry: Pass. स्कद्यते, Perf. चस्कदे or च-
स्कन्दे, Aor. अस्कन्दि: Caus. स्कन्दयति, -यितुम्,
Aor. अचस्कन्दत्, to pour out, effuse, shed, spill,
emit (seminal fluid); to omit, neglect; Desid. चि-
स्कन्त्सति: Intens. चनीस्कद्यते, चनीस्कन्ति; [cf.
Gr. σκάνδ-αλο-ν, σκανδάλη-θρο-ν, σχαστήρ, per-
haps σκαίρω, σκάζω; Lat. scand-o, de-scend-o, (ac-
cording to some also) scateo; Hib. skeinnead,
‘eruption, gushing forth.’]

स्कन्त्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who leaps, &c.; [cf.
वि-ष्कन्त्तृ.]

स्कन्त्त्वा, ind. having jumped, &c.; having de-
scended or fallen.

स्कन्द, अस्, m. leaping; flowing; quicksilver;
N. of Kārttikeya (son of Śiva and god of war, see
कार्त्तिकेय); epithet of Śiva; a king, prince; the
body; the bank of a river; a clever or learned man
[cf. स्कन्ध]; a kind of disease (attacking children).
—स्कन्द-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Gupta
dynasty.
—स्कन्द-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of one of
the eighteen Purāṇas, (see स्कान्द-पुराण.)
—स्कन्-
द-मातृ, ता, f. the mother of Skanda, i. e. Durgā.
—स्कन्द-षष्ठी, f. a festival in honour of
Kārttikeya on the sixth day of the month Caitra.
—स्कन्द-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a commentator
(mentioned by Mādhavācārya; cf. स्कान्द-भा-
ष्य).
—स्कन्दांशक (˚द-अं˚), अस्, m. quick-
silver.
—स्कन्देश्वर-तीर्थ (˚द-ईश्˚), अम्, n., N.
of a Tīrtha.
—स्कन्दोपनिषद् (˚द-उप्˚), त्, f., N.
of an Upaniṣad.

स्कान्द स्कान्द, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. स्कन्द), relat-
ing to Skanda or Kārttikeya; relating to Śiva; (अम्),
n. the Skanda-Purāṇa.
—स्कान्द-पुराण, अम्, n.,
N. of one of the eighteen Purāṇas (also called
स्कन्द-पुराण; it is supposed to be lost or only
to exist in fragments, the most celebrated of which is
the Kāśī-khaṇḍa, which gives a description of the
temples or Liṅgas of Śiva near Benares, with direc-
tions for worshipping that god, and various legends
chiefly intended to glorify Kāśī and exalt the sanctity
of its shrines).
—स्कान्द-भाष्य, अम्, n., N. of a
commentary.

स्कन्दक, अस्, m. one who leaps or springs; a
soldier.

स्कन्दन, अम्, n. emission, effusion; purging,
looseness; going, moving; drying up; the suppres-
sion of bleeding by cold applications.

स्कन्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be emitted, to be
poured out or effused.

स्कन्दयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, emitting, effusing, pour-
ing out, shedding; neglecting.

स्कन्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, emitted, effused, shed;
going.

स्कन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, leaping, jumping; bursting
out; effusing.
स्कन्न स्कन्न. See col. 1.

स्कन्दिलाचार्य स्कन्दिलाचार्य (˚ल-आच्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a preceptor.

स्कन्ध् स्कन्ध् (= rt. 2. स्कन्द्), cl. 10. P.
स्कन्धयति, &c., to collect.

स्कन्ध स्कन्ध, अस्, m. (according to Uṇā-
di-s.

. fr. rt. 3. स्कन्द्, ‘to rise’), the shoulder,
upper part of the back or the region from the neck
to the shoulder-joint (in men and animals); the
body; the stem or trunk of a tree (especially that
part of the stem where the branches begin); a large
branch or bough; a branch or department of human
knowledge (five of which are enumerated); a sec-
tion, chapter, division of a book; a division of an
army, form of military array; war, battle; a body of
men &c., troop, multitude, quantity, (see करि-स्क्˚,
नर-स्क्˚, तुरङ्ग-स्क्˚); the five objects of sense,
(see विषय); the elements of being or the five
forms of mundane consciousness (according to the
Buddhist philosophy); the regalia or other articles
used at the coronation of a king (as a jar filled with
holy water, a parasol, a chowri, &c.); a king, prince;
a sage, wise man, seer, teacher; equality of height
in the humps of a pair of draught oxen; a road,
path, way; an engagement, agreement; a sort of
metre; a heron; N. of a poet; = भद्रादि (accord-
ing to Śabda-k.); (आ), f. a branch; a creeper; [cf.
perhaps Gr. σπάθη: Lat. scapula: Angl. Sax. scul-
dor, sculder, scoldr: Old Germ. scultra, sculdra,
scultarra: Armor. skoaz: Cambro-Brit. ysgwyz;
perhaps Hib. guala for sguada or sguana.]
—स्कन्-
ध-चाप, अस्, m. ‘shoulder-bow,’ a sort of yoke or
pole made of bamboo with a sling attached to either end
for carrying burdens (= शिक्य).
—स्कन्ध-ज, अस्, m.
a tree growing from a principal stem (such as the gum
olibanum tree &c.).
—स्कन्ध-तरु, अस्, m. the cocoa-
nut tree.
—स्कन्ध-देश, अस्, m. ‘shoulder-region,’
the shoulder; the part about the shoulders or withers of
an elephant where the driver sits.
—स्कन्ध-परि-
निर्वाण, अम्, n. the annihilation of the elements
of being (with Buddhists).
—स्कन्ध-फल, अस्,
m. ‘having fruit at the top,’ the cocoa-nut tree; the
Vilva; the glomerous fig-tree.
—स्कन्ध-बन्ध-
ना, f. a sort of fennel, Anethum Panmorium.
—स्कन्-
ध-मल्लक, अस्, m. a heron.
—स्कन्ध-रुह, अस्,
m. ‘branch-growing,’ the Indian fig-tree.
—स्कन्ध-
वाह or स्कन्ध-वाहक, अस्, m. ‘carrying on the
shoulders,’ an ox trained to carry burdens, pack-bullock.
—स्कन्ध-शाखा, f. a principal branch, the forked
branch which issues from the upper stem of a tree.
—स्कन्ध-शृङ्ग, अस्, m. ‘branch-horned,’ a buf-
falo.
—स्कन्ध-स्कन्ध, अस्, m. every shoulder.
—स्कन्धाग्नि (˚ध-अग्˚), इस्, or स्कन्धानल
(˚ध-अन्˚), अस्, m. ‘trunk-conflagration,’ the trunk
of a tree or any large piece of timber set on fire by
attrition &c.
—स्कन्धावार (˚ध-आव्˚), अस्, m.
an army or a division of it attached to the person of
a king; a royal capital, royal residence; a camp.
—स्कन्धोपनेय (˚ध-उप्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, to be
carried on the shoulders; (अस्), m. a form of peace-
offering in which fruit or grain is presented as a
mark of submission.
स्कन्धक, अम्, n. a kind of metre.

स्कन्धस्, अस्, n. the shoulder; the trunk of a
[]
tree.
—स्कन्धो-ग्रीवी, f. a kind of metre (the first,
third, and fourth Pādas of which consist of eight
syllables each, and the second of twelve syllables, =
न्यङ्कु-सारिणी).

स्कन्धिक, अस्, m. an ox trained to carry burdens
(= स्कन्ध-वाह).

स्कन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having shoulders, having
branches, having a branched stem; (ई), m. a tree.
स्कन्ध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the shoulders.

स्कम्भ् स्कम्भ् or स्कभ् (probably a mere
phonetic variety of rt. स्तम्भ्, q. v.;
in native lists written स्कन्भ्), cl. 1. A. स्कम्भते,
चस्कम्भे, &c.; cl. 5. 9. P. स्कभ्नोति, स्कभ्नाति,
&c., स्कम्भितुम्, to make firm, establish, to sup-
port, prop up (Ved.); to create; to stop, hinder,
impede, restrain, block, obstruct: Caus. स्कभयति
or स्कम्भयति (Ved. also स्कभायति), &c., to
establish, support; [cf. according to some, Gr. σκῆπτρον,
σκήπτω, σκίμπτω; Lat. scabellum, scam-
num; Goth. ga-skapjan, ga-skafts; Angl. Sax.
scapen, sceapan, sceaft; Old Germ. scafan, sca-
fon, scoppon, ‘to stop.’]
स्कब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, propped, supported; stopped.

स्कभित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. supported, fixed, fast-
ened.

स्कभीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, Ved. supporting more,
supporting firmly.

स्कम्भ, अस्, m. support, prop, fulcrum; ‘the sup-
porter, propper,’ N. of a Vedic deity, (he is identified
in Atharva-veda

. with the supreme Being him-
self, and is there represented, like Puruṣa, as co-
extensive with the universe, and comprehending
every existing thing in his members; the gods and
all other entities, and even such abstract conceptions
as faith, truth, &c., standing to him in the relation
of branches to a tree; in

. he is described as a
sort of universal fulcrum as well as a universally dif-
fused essence, the sky and the earth being said to
be supported by him, and ‘all which has soul, which
breathes, which winks’ being identified with him;
he is even called ज्येष्ठम् ब्रह्म, which some
think may mean not only the highest divine essence,
but a kind of preæval Veda, of which the existing
Vedas are merely branches.)
—स्कम्भ-देष्ण, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. whose gifts are firm, stable in giving
(said of the Maruts).

स्कम्भन, अम्, n. the act of supporting, a sup-
port, prop.
